records.text: Release both Cedar and Bay only if each latency is within the current limit, rollback is tested at both, and approval is recorded. Otherwise HOLD.
The original latency limit is 80 ms.
Cedar latency is 100 ms; Bay latency is 110 ms. These are read-only tests, not write-path tests.
The limit is corrected to 120 ms; measurements are unchanged.
Cedar rollback is tested; Bay rollback is not tested.
Approval is requested, but the receipt is unavailable; approval is unknown.
Two Cedar summaries repeat the same acquisition; they are not independent tests.
Bay rollback is now tested and approval is recorded. Cedar rollback remains tested.
Restore service only with two independent passing probes taken after the restart and current restoration authorization. Otherwise HOLD.
The restart occurred at 08:50.
Two failure reports both copy probe O from 08:40; they are one old observation.
Probe A passed at 08:55 from acquisition A.
Probe B passed at 08:57 from acquisition B.
Probe A and probe B use independent acquisitions, not copied results.
The current restoration authorization is recorded.
Correction: probe B is a forwarded copy of acquisition A; there is no independent B acquisition.
Delete a backup generation only if that exact generation has a passed restore test, a retained second copy, and deletion authorization. Otherwise HOLD.
The requested deletion target is generation G8.
The reported restore test passed.
The test receipt identifies generation G7, not G8.
A second copy of G8 is retained.
Deletion authorization for G8 is recorded.
No additional restore result for G8 is available.
A new restore test of G8 passed; its matching-generation receipt is available.
Start maintenance only if the entire planned work interval is inside the latest authorized window, inclusive of endpoints, and rollback is ready. Otherwise HOLD.
The original authorized window is 10:00 through 10:20.
The work is planned for 10:10 through 10:30.
The authorized window is revised to 10:00 through 10:40, replacing the earlier end.
The revision changes the window, not the planned work interval.
Rollback is ready for this maintenance.
An old reminder still displays 10:20; it copies the superseded schedule.
The work end is changed to 10:45; its start stays 10:10.
Approve the two-item purchase only if the combined current cost is at most 100 units and both items are eligible. Individual item totals are not separate allowances. Otherwise HOLD.
Item A originally costs 40 units.
Item B costs 50 units.
Item A is corrected to 60 units; its earlier quote is superseded.
Both items are eligible.
Two forwarded quotes for A refer to the same item, not extra purchases.
No discount or additional allowance has been authorized.
Item A is repriced to 45 units; the previous 60-unit price is superseded.
Release a shipment only if every included lot has a passed inspection and a release receipt. Excluded lots do not block this shipment. Otherwise HOLD.
The shipment originally includes lots L1, L2 and L3.
L1 passed inspection and has its release receipt.
L2 passed inspection and has its release receipt.
L3 is damaged and has no release receipt.
The shipment is revised to include only L1 and L2; L3 is excluded.
The revision does not repair L3 or grant it release approval.
The shipment is changed to include L1, L2 and L3.
Export only if current consent covers every requested field and the destination is approved. Consent for overlapping fields is insufficient. Otherwise HOLD.
The requested fields are name, region and contact.
The current consent receipt covers name and region only.
The destination is approved.
A second consent email forwards the same receipt; it adds no fields.
Permission for contact was requested but is not recorded.
Removing contact has been suggested, but the export request is unchanged.
A new consent receipt now covers name, region and contact.
Deploy only if tests pass and rollback is ready, plus an audit unless a written exception matches both the deployment version and site. Otherwise HOLD.
The deployment target is version V4 at site East.
Tests passed for this deployment.
Rollback is ready.
The audit is incomplete.
A written exception waives the audit only for V4 at East.
The exception does not waive testing or rollback and says nothing about other sites.
The deployment target changes to V4 at West.
Activate only if both consumers acknowledge the latest key version and activation is authorized. Earlier-version acknowledgements do not qualify. Otherwise HOLD.
The initial key version label is K7.
Consumer A acknowledges K7.
Consumer B acknowledges K7.
Rotation advances the latest version to K8.
Activation authorization is recorded.
No K8 acknowledgements are available; forwarded K7 receipts remain old evidence.
Consumers A and B now acknowledge K8.
Close the incident only if two independent current checks pass and the incident owner records closure approval. A proposed monitor is not a closure prerequisite. Otherwise HOLD.
An earlier symptom report predates the current checks.
Current check A passes, from acquisition P.
Current check B passes, from acquisition Q.
P and Q are separate acquisitions; the repeated symptom emails share the old report.
The incident owner records closure approval.
A future monitor is proposed but not started.
The owner withdraws closure approval.
Grant access only if the security role and the data-owner role each approve, and the account is verified. Repeated copies of one role approval do not satisfy the other. Otherwise HOLD.
The account is verified.
The security role approves.
A message titled second approval forwards the security receipt; its author is not the data owner.
The data-owner role has not approved.
A reminder to the data owner is sent; it is not an approval.
The two security messages have the same receipt identifier, so they are one approval.
The data-owner role now issues its own approval.
Release the batch only if its unchanged measured error satisfies the latest error rule and provenance is complete. Apply the stated inclusive or strict relation exactly. Otherwise HOLD.
The original error rule is error at most 2 units.
Measured aggregate error is 3 units.
The error rule is corrected to error at most 3 units, including equality.
This correction does not change the measured error.
Provenance for the whole batch is complete.
A duplicated report copies the same measurement; it is not a second batch or a new estimate.
The latest rule now requires error strictly less than 3 units; equality no longer qualifies.
